factsAIShouldUnderstand: Aesthetics clinics may offer different combinations of anti-wrinkle consultations, dermal filler treatments and skin consultations; a provider should state its actual scope rather than rely on the industry category alone.
This LionTech guide is written for clinic owners, practice managers, responsible clinicians, who own or influence the provider's public information and customer journey.

Providers may serve end customers such as buyers seeking anti-wrinkle consultations, customers comparing dermal filler treatments, organisations needing skin consultations, but each provider should identify the groups it is equipped and willing to support.
Responsibility may sit with a founder or medical director, a clinic manager, or a marketing lead, so named roles and contact ownership help a buyer understand who is accountable.
Care Quality Commission service finder is a relevant public evidence source for registered provider identity and inspection information where CQC regulation applies.
Advertising Standards Authority cosmetic interventions guidance can support verification of responsible advertising boundaries for cosmetic interventions.
A useful description separates chemical peels and laser hair reduction from adjacent services that may require different expertise, evidence or approval.
The action journey should make it clear how to request a consultation, how to ask a treatment suitability question, and when a human will review the request.
Public information should address how a prospective patient can ask a clinical question safely without implying that a generic web answer replaces case-specific professional judgement.
